payload.body:
## Verdict
Changes requested

## Blockers

1. **F1 — A concurrent create can be overwritten without a backup.** Start `/files/upload?overwrite=1` for an absent target, then create that target through another request while the upload body is streaming. [writeFileAtomic](/tmp/wt-up-files-journal/src/file-guard.js:660) makes a trash backup only when the target existed at its initial check, but [the overwrite commit](/tmp/wt-up-files-journal/src/file-guard.js:664) always uses `renameSync`. The later upload can silently destroy the newly created file and return 200, violating the recoverable overwrite contract in [protocol.md](/tmp/wt-up-files-journal/docs/protocol.md:2488). At commit, use a no-clobber install when the target was initially absent; otherwise preserve and verify the current target before replacing it.

   ## Tags: [rollback-unsound]

   ```json
   {
     "finding_id": "F1",
     "severity": "blocker",
     "ship_blocking": true,
     "requires_operator_judgement": false,
     "out_of_scope_load_bearing": false,
     "defect_class": "rollback-unsound",
     "area": "src/file-guard.js",
     "short_label": "Concurrent create loses its file",
     "normalized_text": "Trigger: an overwrite-enabled upload starts while its target is absent, and another request creates the target before the upload finishes streaming. writeFileAtomic backs up only a target present at preparation (src/file-guard.js:660), then unconditionally renames over the destination when overwrite is true (src/file-guard.js:664-667). The concurrent file is replaced without a trash link, yet the upload returns success. Both upload and JSON write call this primitive (src/files-write-http.js:294,358). Use a no-clobber commit for an initially absent target, or preserve and verify the file present at commit before replacement."
   }
   ```

2. **F2 — Revocation during an upload does not stop its commit.** Authorization is checked at route entry and at the start of [audited](/tmp/wt-up-files-journal/src/files-write-http.js:125), before [the upload body is consumed](/tmp/wt-up-files-journal/src/files-write-http.js:291). If the user is demoted or the device revoked while a slow upload is streaming, the guard can still commit the file and return 200. This breaks the immediate revocation behavior promised in [protocol.md](/tmp/wt-up-files-journal/docs/protocol.md:2448). Recheck the live user and device immediately before the filesystem commit, after the body has finished.

   ## Tags: [gate-audit-incomplete]

   ```json
   {
     "finding_id": "F2",
     "severity": "blocker",
     "ship_blocking": true,
     "requires_operator_judgement": false,
     "out_of_scope_load_bearing": false,
     "defect_class": "gate-audit-incomplete",
     "area": "src/files-write-http.js",
     "short_label": "Revoked upload can still commit",
     "normalized_text": "Trigger: an authorized client begins a slow POST /files/upload, then its admin flag is removed or its device is revoked before the body finishes. The second authorization check runs when audited starts (src/files-write-http.js:125-128); the body is consumed later (src/files-write-http.js:291-295), and writeFileAtomic commits after that without another authorization check. The observable outcome can be a 200 and a changed host file after revocation, contrary to docs/protocol.md:2448-2449. Pass a commit-time authorization check into the streamed write path and refuse before installation if it fails."
   }
   ```

3. **F3 — A credential file can be downloaded from a configured read root.** The sensitive-name patterns omit `.pypirc`; `isSensitivePath('~/.pypirc')` returns `false`. With a read root containing that credential file, [openGuarded](/tmp/wt-up-files-journal/src/file-guard.js:1473) passes it to [the content route](/tmp/wt-up-files-journal/src/http.js:391), which streams its bytes. This violates the stated credential exclusion in [protocol.md](/tmp/wt-up-files-journal/docs/protocol.md:2456). Add `.pypirc` to the shared sensitive-path rule and test listing, metadata, and content access through the real routes.

   ## Tags: [path-coverage-regression]

   ```json
   {
     "finding_id": "F3",
     "severity": "blocker",
     "ship_blocking": true,
     "requires_operator_judgement": false,
     "out_of_scope_load_bearing": false,
     "defect_class": "path-coverage-regression",
     "area": "src/file-guard.js",
     "short_label": "PyPI credential file remains readable",
     "normalized_text": "Trigger: a configured read root contains a .pypirc file with a package-index credential, and an authorized client requests it through /files/content. The basename denylist omits .pypirc (src/file-guard.js:36-79); isSensitivePath returns false, so openGuarded's sensitive check at src/file-guard.js:1473 does not refuse it. The content handler streams the validated descriptor at src/http.js:391-472. A read root therefore exposes credential bytes despite the explicit exclusion in docs/protocol.md:2456-2459. Add this credential filename to the common guard and exercise all three read routes against it."
   }
   ```
